clue.text: Bloody thick, this leader of council group

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of council
a lot is a group or batch of things

explanation.surface: Someone swears at the dim-witted head of a council faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody thick' reads as a British insult, but it describes blood that has thickened into a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is a congealed mass of blood; the word is also slang for a stupid person, which feeds the surface.

clue.text: Make a hit: say yes to opening of trousers

blocks.note: to let something happen is to permit it
the fly is the zipped opening at the front of trousers

explanation.surface: Seduction advice: agree when someone reaches for your zip and you have scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is to lash out or strike at someone, so it means to land a blow.

clue.text: Celebs who keep their distance may nevertheless be taken with this

definitions.text: Celebs who keep their distance may nevertheless be taken with this

blocks.clueFragment: Celebs who keep their distance may nevertheless be taken with this
blocks.note: surface reading: a charm or appeal that wins over even aloof stars
setter's reading: photographed by paparazzi using a long-range camera lens

explanation.surface: Even stand-offish celebrities may be smitten by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken with' suggests being charmed; here it means photographed, by a lens that works from far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens magnifies distant subjects, the paparazzi's tool for snapping stars who stay well away.

clue.text: Satisfy yourself mother's butter is runny without one

indicators.note: something runny has lost its shape and flows into a new form
without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around another

blocks.note: MA is mother, plus the S of the possessive
taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A cheeky domestic scene: Mum's butter has gone soft, so fend for yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside: the jumbled butter goes round the letter for one.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy yourself is a euphemism for self-pleasuring, which the answer names directly.

clue.text: Electoral authority also welcomed by China

indicators.note: something welcomed by a host is taken inside it

blocks.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A political report that Beijing has also endorsed an election result.
explanation.walkthrough: China is not the country but Cockney rhyming slang for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is the authority a government claims from winning an election.

clue.text: (& 19ac.) John Sergeant's decision to quit Strictly Come Dancing? Certainly not any of his dance steps!

definitions.text: John Sergeant's decision to quit Strictly Come Dancing

blocks.clueFragment: John Sergeant's decision to quit Strictly Come Dancing
blocks.note: surface reading: a wise choice by the journalist to leave the TV dance contest

blocks.clueFragment: Certainly not any of his dance steps
blocks.note: setter's reading: none of his clumsy routines could be called elegant footwork

explanation.surface: A dig at the portly broadcaster who quit a celebrity dance show while being kept in by the public vote.
explanation.walkthrough: John Sergeant, a BBC political journalist, walked off Strictly Come Dancing in 2008; the answer praises the exit and mocks the dancing in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever decision is a shrewd step, while a polished dance step would be neat footwork; the phrase fits only the exit.

clue.text: Lots have sex (not head, though), a number taking stimulant

indicators.note: with no head, the word loses its opening letter
a number taking something holds it inside

blocks.note: to hump is slang for having sex
ten is a number
E is ecstasy, a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: Plenty of people are having sex, many of them on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: HUMP loses its H, then TEN takes in E: UMP + TEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a large but unspecified quantity.

clue.text: Stink raised by body over Australian low grade plonk

blocks.note: BO is body odour
Oz is slang for Australia
E is a low mark on an exam

explanation.surface: A wine critic sniffs at a cheap Australian red.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places one piece above the next. Plonk is British slang for cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonk is cheap wine, a kind of alcoholic drink, so it is a specific case of booze.

clue.text: Drop behind a human dynamo

blocks.note: a tear is a drop from the eye
behind means backside, arse in British slang

explanation.surface: An instruction to let a dynamic person get ahead of you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word but is the backside itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear-arse is British slang for someone who rushes about full of energy, like a dynamo.

clue.text: Hot when woman's scarf nudges middle of penis

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its single central letter

blocks.note: a stole is a woman's shawl or scarf
the central letter of penis

explanation.surface: Things get heated when a woman's scarf brushes against a man's crotch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods that have been stolen and are risky to sell on.

clue.text: What Brown seeks for his policies? Papal dispensation about love in recreational vehicle

definitions.text: What Brown seeks for his policies?

indicators.note: a dispensation is a dealing-out, so the letters are distributed afresh
about means around, so these letters surround the rest
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
RV is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown hoping the Pope will bless his programme, picturing love in a camper van.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was the UK Prime Minister at the time; 'Papal dispensation' reads as a church ruling but is an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician seeks public endorsement of his programme, which is what approval means.

clue.text: Snap a heavy breather's thing? Cheeky!

a heavy breather's thing is to pant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' suggests a photo and 'thing' suggests anatomy; both are red herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means lacking proper respect or seriousness, close in sense to impertinent.

clue.text: Seamen flustered into forced evacuations

indicators.note: flustered means thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Panicking sailors are herded into an emergency evacuation of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuations' suggests clearing people off a ship; it is the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema flushes out the bowel by injected fluid, an evacuation brought about artificially.

clue.text: (& 14ac.) They offer an advantageous purchase to overweight lovers

definitions.text: They offer an advantageous purchase to overweight lovers

blocks.note: surface reading: a shop deal or bargain for plump couples
setter's reading: purchase means grip, something a partner can grasp during sex

explanation.surface: A shop offering a good deal to chubby couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' means a firm grip, not something bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Love handles are rolls of fat at the waist, jokingly named as something a partner can grip.

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the Queen is spoken of as Her

the last letter of flunkey

clue.text: Bastard Conservative in terribly evil hold

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bastard' looks like an insult for the Tory; it is the literal meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A love child is a child born to unmarried parents, the literal sense of bastard.

clue.text: After drink, Brenda's a belter!

Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, ER

explanation.surface: After a few drinks, the Queen turns out to be a terrific singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belter' suggests a loud singer or a great thing; here it is someone who belts, or hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A walloper is someone who strikes hard, as is a belter in the sense of one who belts.

clue.text: One more pervert on earth

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A weary complaint that yet another deviant walks the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' looks like a noun, a deviant; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one, one more of the same kind.

clue.text: Over-promoted, extremely hammy deputy given a rise and feeling good

in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the outside letters of hammy
dep is the abbreviation for deputy
to feel up is to be in good spirits

explanation.definitionFit: Hyped up means publicised or promoted beyond its merit, exaggerated by advertising.

clue.text: see 5dn.
see 14dn.

clue.text: (& 27ac.) Substitute model of inflation that offers some relief?

clue.text: Paddy-driven social Lib-Lab pact's description?
